_about: Starter band and library for improv (SPR-I.2.2). Imported once by manage.py seed_improv_library; after that the database rows are the data, this file is never read again by the app. Progressions are generic patterns, not named songs. Groove shapes are documented in docs/improv/data_model.md under Style. Drum grids are 16 steps for a 4/4 bar, one step per sixteenth, value 0 to 1 is the hit strength. Charts follow the grammar in docs/improv/api.md.

progressions.title: ii-V-I in major
progressions.description: The most common move in jazz. Dm7 is the ii, G7 the V that pulls toward home, Cmaj7 the I where it rests. Hear the leading tones: F falls to E, B rises to C.

progressions.title: ii-V-I in minor
progressions.description: The minor version: a half-diminished ii, an altered V, a minor tonic. The V has more tension to play with, so the resolution sounds bigger.

progressions.title: I-vi-ii-V turnaround
progressions.description: Four bars that lead back to the start, so they loop forever. The root motion is a falling fifth, a step, a falling fifth.

progressions.title: Diatonic circle of fifths
progressions.chart: | Cmaj7 | Fmaj7 | Bm7b5 | E7alt | Am7 | Dm7 | G7 | Cmaj7 |
progressions.description: Every chord is a fifth below the last and stays in one key, except the E7 that borrows an altered dominant to lead into Am. Eight bars of voice leading.

progressions.title: Minor circle ii-V-I
progressions.chart: | Cm7 | F7 | Bbmaj7 | Ebmaj7 | Am7b5 | D7alt | Gm7 | % |
progressions.description: A major ii-V-I that lands on the relative major, then a minor ii-V-I that lands on the minor home. Two keys in one eight-bar loop.

progressions.title: Rhythm changes, A section
progressions.chart: |: Bbmaj7 G7 | Cm7 F7 | Dm7 G7 | Cm7 F7 | Fm7 Bb7 | Ebmaj7 Edim7 | Dm7 G7 | [1 Cm7 F7 :| [2 Bbmaj7 |
progressions.description: The A section of the most-played pattern in jazz, written with a repeat and two endings. Fast, two chords in most bars, so the changes arrive every two beats.

progressions.title: Dorian modal vamp
progressions.description: One chord for eight bars, then the same chord a half step up. No changes to follow, so the whole job is shaping a line over one sound and then moving it.

progressions.title: Key change up a whole step
progressions.chart: {key: C} | Dm7 | G7 | Cmaj7 | % | {key: Eb} | Fm7 | Bb7 | Ebmaj7 | % |
progressions.description: A ii-V-I in C, then the same shape in Eb. Practise carrying the idea you just played into the new key.

progressions.title: Twelve-bar blues
progressions.description: Three chords, twelve bars, every chord a dominant. The oldest form there is. Start with the blues scale and listen for the turn into the last two bars.

progressions.title: Jazz blues
progressions.chart: | C7 | F7 | C7 | Gm7 C7 | F7 | Fdim7 | C7 | A7alt | Dm7 | G7 | C7 A7alt | Dm7 G7 |
progressions.description: The twelve bars with the jazz changes put in: a ii-V into the IV, a passing diminished chord, a secondary dominant, and a turnaround.

progressions.title: Minor blues
progressions.chart: | Cm7 | % | % | % | Fm7 | % | Cm7 | % | Ab7 | G7alt | Cm7 | G7alt |
progressions.description: Twelve bars in minor. The pentatonic minor scale works over all of it; the Ab7 and G7 in the last four bars are where to listen.

progressions.title: Pop four chords
progressions.description: I, V, vi, IV. Thousands of songs run on it. Good for playing melodic phrases with room to breathe.

progressions.title: Fifties changes
progressions.description: I, vi, IV, V. The old doo-wop loop. Simple chords, so the rhythm of your line is what matters.

progressions.title: Bossa ii-V-I loop
progressions.description: A ii-V-I whose last bar turns back toward the start with an A7. Straight eighths, so long even lines sound right.

progressions.title: Gospel eight bars
progressions.chart: | C | C/E | F | Fm | C/G | Am7 | Dm7 G7 | C |
progressions.description: A slow shuffle with a walking bass line (C, E, F, then the minor iv chord) and a cadence that lands home. The Fm is the soulful turn.

progressions.title: Tritone-sub ii-V-I
progressions.description: The V chord swapped for the dominant a tritone away. Db7 shares the two notes that define G7 (its F, and its B written as Cb), so the bass slides down by a half step into home.

progressions.title: Backdoor ii-V
progressions.description: The minor iv and the bVII dominant arriving at home from above instead of below. A softer landing than the ordinary V, with the same Cmaj7 at the end.

progressions.title: iii-vi-ii-V
progressions.description: A longer way round the circle of fifths than the plain turnaround, landing on home at the end. The A7 is a borrowed dominant of the Dm7 that follows it.

progressions.title: Minor turnaround
progressions.description: A turnaround for a minor tune: the tonic, a half-diminished step, and the minor ii-V that brings it back round.

progressions.title: Secondary dominant run
progressions.chart: | Cmaj7 | E7 | Am7 | C7 | Fmaj7 | D7 | Dm7 G7 | Cmaj7 |
progressions.description: Each minor or major chord is approached by its own dominant: E7 to Am7, C7 to Fmaj7, D7 to the ii-V. Eight bars that sound like a small tune.

progressions.title: Major thirds cycle
progressions.chart: | Cmaj7 Eb7 | Abmaj7 B7 | Emaj7 G7 | Cmaj7 | % |
progressions.description: Three tonal centres a major third apart: C, Ab and E. The hardest pattern in the library. Slow first, and name the centre you are in.

progressions.title: Dorian groove
progressions.description: Two chords, two bars each. Over the Dm7 play D Dorian, a natural 6 against the minor third; the G7 is the IV7 that makes Dorian sound like itself.

progressions.title: Lydian vamp
progressions.description: A major chord on the second step over a held C bass. The F# in the D chord is the sound of C Lydian.

progressions.title: Quick-change blues
progressions.description: The twelve-bar blues with the IV chord stepped in at bar two. The one most players hear in their heads first.

progressions.title: Slow blues with ninths
progressions.description: A slow twelve with fuller chords and a turnaround of its own. Room for long bends of the line and for leaving space.

progressions.title: Eight-bar blues
progressions.description: Eight bars instead of twelve: the form arrives sooner, so there is less time to settle.

progressions.title: Descending pop line
progressions.chart: | C | G/B | Am | Em/G | F | C/E | Dm7 | G |
progressions.description: The bass walks down a step at a time while the chords above it are simple triads. Keep the right hand to the notes of each chord and listen to the bass.

progressions.title: Minor pop loop
progressions.description: The four chords of the pop loop, started from the minor chord. The same chords as the major version, a different home.

progressions.title: Suspended pop ballad
progressions.description: The G suspends the C of the tonic for half a bar before it resolves. The Fadd9 adds a G on top for a bright, open sound.

progressions.title: Rock I, bVII, IV
progressions.description: The chord on the flat seventh is the sound of C Mixolydian, a major scale with a b7. Use the Bb as the clue.

progressions.title: Rock minor, bVII and bVI
progressions.description: The natural minor scale played as chords. Every chord is in A natural minor, so one scale covers the whole loop.

progressions.title: Andalusian descent
progressions.description: Four chords stepping down from the minor tonic and ending on a major E, which pulls back to Am. The G# in the E chord is the piece that is not in the scale.

progressions.title: Gospel turnaround
progressions.chart: | C | E7 | Am7 | C7 | F | Fm | C/G | G7 |
progressions.description: The E7 and the C7 each push the next chord, the Fm is the soulful turn, and the G7 carries you round again.

progressions.title: Gospel plagal vamp
progressions.chart: | C | F/C | C | F/C | Am7 | Dm7 | G7sus4 G7 | C |
progressions.description: The amen cadence rocks over a held C, then a ii-V closes the eight bars. Leave room for the pause on the G7sus4.

progressions.title: Bossa minor ii-V-i
progressions.description: A minor ii-V-i with a bar of the tonic on each side. The straight eighths of the groove suit long, even lines.

progressions.title: Bossa eight bars
progressions.chart: | Cmaj7 | Dm7 G7 | Em7 A7 | Dm7 G7 | Cmaj7 | Fmaj7 | Dm7 G7 | Cmaj7 |
progressions.description: Eight bars with a ii-V in nearly every one. Slow enough to land a chord tone on each change.

progressions.title: Minor montuno vamp
progressions.description: A tonic and a dominant going back and forth. Practice short phrases that end on the beat.

progressions.title: Funk one chord
progressions.description: One dominant ninth chord and nothing else. All the interest is in the rhythm of what you play, not in the harmony.

progressions.title: Dorian funk
progressions.description: A minor seventh and a dominant thirteenth, two bars each. Dorian over the first, Mixolydian over the second.

progressions.title: Funk four-bar groove
progressions.description: A minor tonic, its IV9, and a flat-seven dominant that comes back to the start. Short, tight phrases land best.
